Anna (eng-runtime): noticing a p99 spike across eu-west-2 embed endpoints since the CUDA14 driver rollout ~30m ago. p95 up a bit but p99 jumped ~3-4x. Anyone else seeing this?
Mike (eng-infra): yup seeing it on host telemetry too — NVMe iowait and disk qdepth are higher on gpu nodes that got the driver.
Tariq (eng-sre): alert fired: /alerts/p99-latency/eu-west-2. Linking quick dashboards.
Olivia (support): customer ACME reported degraded throughput, they opened a ticket referencing 12:15 UTC. Escalating to infra.
Denis (eng-ml): did model config change? We didn't change grouping/batching. Looks like runtime is stalling on host IO during KV cache loads.
Mike (eng-infra): ran perf and iostat. sample: 
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.0   400.0  51200  204800  0.00   0.00   25.30  0.95  55.00
```
Queue depth spikes correlate with long GPU attach operations.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4076543210 (severity: high)
Anna (eng-runtime): confirmed we observe long stalls during KV cache refill path where we read prefixes from disk. Likely host IO regression after driver+firmware combo interacting with kernel io scheduler.
Tariq (eng-sre): can someone run fio on an impacted host to reproduce tail latency? Run read pattern with random access and 4k blocks:
```
fio --name=nvme-tail --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=64 --direct=1 --numjobs=8 --runtime=60
```
Mike (eng-infra): running now. preliminary fio tail: 99.99th = 350ms, baseline before rollout was ~6ms. So definitely regressed.
Denis (eng-ml): are GPUs showing any firmware errors? GPU logs look clean but there are intermittent NVMe timeout messages in dmesg around the same time as stalls.
Mike (eng-infra): dmesg snippet: 
```
[  123.456789] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 0 timeout, aborting
[  123.457012] nvme nvme0: reset controller
```
Kernel version: 6.6.4, Driver: nvidia-driver 554.12 + CUDA14 runtime. This combination was rolled to eu-west-2 nodes at 11:50 UTC.
Olivia (support): I told ACME we're investigating and asked for any useful request IDs. They sent a few sample request IDs (rids: r_9a3f, r_9a4b).
Anna (eng-runtime): pulled traces for r_9a3f — shows long blocking on cache read syscall (pread) waiting ~280ms. We do fallback to model variant if KV cache misses exceed threshold but threshold isn't hit quickly because stall pattern is bursty.
Tariq (eng-sre): short-term mitigations: 1) pin affected traffic away from eu-west-2 via routing rule, 2) rollback driver on a canary pool, 3) reduce iodepth on runtime read path to avoid queue buildup. Which is fastest?
Mike (eng-infra): rollback on a small canary pool is the fastest to validate. I can coordinate rollback for 20 nodes. Also can tweak elevator to mq-deadline and set nr_requests per queue lower.
Anna (eng-runtime): we can quickly deploy a config change: cap KV read iodepth to 8 for recovering requests. That should reduce tail but will increase average slightly. I'll prepare a canary config.
deploy-bot: rollout started: runtime-config/kv-io-cap -> canary (10% nodes)
Tariq (eng-sre): Mike — please run rollback on 5 nodes first, and run fio again to compare.
Mike (eng-infra): rolling back driver on canary 5 nodes now. Command: 
```
sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-550.80 -y && reboot
```
(doing controlled reboot sequence)
Anna (eng-runtime): applying iodepth cap in canary now. Patch: ``KV_IO_MAX_DEPTH=8`` on canary.
~20m later~
Mike (eng-infra): fio on rolled-back nodes: p99 tail = 8.6ms. Non-rolled nodes still 320ms. Good signal rollback fixes it.
Anna (eng-runtime): runtime saw p99 drop back down on canary traffic. Will keep cap while we validate full rollback.
Tariq (eng-sre): mitigation plan: 1) ramp rollback to all affected nodes in eu-west-2 over next 2 hours, 2) keep KV_IO_MAX_DEPTH=8 cluster-wide for 6 hours as safety net, 3) vendor engage with NVIDIA on driver+nvme interaction, collect logs and reproduce on bench.
Olivia (support): updated ACME: temporary routing to other regions for their critical traffic and we are rolling back drivers in eu-west-2; next update in 60m.
Denis (eng-ml): also suggest we add a runtime circuit-breaker: if pread latency > 100ms for 5 consecutive requests, bypass disk and serve from smaller warm cache model or throttle requests. I'll draft PR.
Anna (eng-runtime): agreed — add circuit-breaker PR and add an eval metric for KV read tail latency.
Tariq (eng-sre): postmortem checklist: capture node-level metrics (iostat, nvme-cli logs, dmesg), driver versions, kernel versions, exact firmware, fio artifacts, and records of rollout windows. We'll create INC-2026-4076543210/postmortem.
Mike (eng-infra): initiating rollback ramp now. I'll post progress updates.
Olivia (support): thanks team — keeping customer updated. Will post final after rollback completes. :thumbsup:
